quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving on an open highway, you should signal to turn ____ before you begin turning.
questions.explanation: Signal to warn other drivers when you change lanes or turn. On an open highway, start your signal at least 300 feet before you turn. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: Are placed everywhere there is danger.
Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black text on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. These signs show speed limits, no passing rules, no turning rules, and other driving regulations.

questions.question: When may you honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: It is proper to use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. Sound your horn to alert other drivers of the danger.

questions.question: To pass a slower car on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the lane meant for oncoming traffic to complete your pass. Only pass if you can do so safely and legally.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: In many crashes with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians, drivers said they were looking but did not see them. These are harder to spot because they are smaller, move faster, and have less noticeable lights. Always watch for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians to prevent crashes.

questions.question: There may be times when 10 mph is too fast to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Drive slower than the posted speed limit when safety requires it. Bad traffic, weather, or poor visibility may require you to drive as slowly as 10 miles per hour.

questions.question: When driving 40 mph or slower, stay at least ____ behind the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: When driving at 40 mph or slower, keep at least two seconds of distance behind the vehicle in front of you. This is the minimum recommended distance. You can increase it when possible for extra safety.

questions.question: On a non-freeway road, drivers should look ahead at least ____ seconds.
questions.explanation: On a non-freeway road, always look at least 12 seconds ahead of your vehicle. On a freeway, look 20 to 30 seconds ahead. Looking ahead helps you avoid sudden stops or turns.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
When driving in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt normal traffic flow. You can receive a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Require a tune-up sooner than normal.
Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases, reduces noise, and cools hot gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust can be deadly very quickly. They can also make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never walk into a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Walk into a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when it is convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never walk into a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not walk into a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle coming from close by may not have time to stop.

questions.question: It is unlawful for a car to try to share a lane with a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Two motorcycles can share a lane, but cars cannot share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, which vehicle must yield?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right. This rule applies to intersections with signs, signals, or no controls.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Always check your mirrors and use your turn signal before you start to change lanes.

questions.question: This sign means that:

options.text: A community group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through this work zone.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has three or more curves.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes use arrows to control turns from certain lanes. A solid red arrow means:

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow has the same meaning as a red circular traffic light. Drivers must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits an unattended parked car and you cannot find the owner. You:

options.text: Have done all you need to do.
Must wait for the police to arrive.
Must leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened in the accident.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed. Do not turn right where you see this sign.

questions.question: You cannot parallel park within ____ of a fire hydrant.
questions.explanation: Do not parallel park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Park only in legal spaces where other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. You should:

options.text: Drive slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Do not enter the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Use your horn to make cars move forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up and you cannot drive completely through it. Wait until traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle downhill on a two-way street:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the greater the impact force if you crash.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following, except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. It is not affected by your physical fitness level or how well you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in determining your vehicle's stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to turn than passenger vehicles.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on all sides—front, sides, and rear. Avoid staying in these areas. Trucks also need more room to turn and stop than passenger vehicles because of their size and weight.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Blow your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.
Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, blow your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle is coming at you head-on, first honk your horn. If the other driver does not move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left—if the other driver corrects at the last second, you will still crash. Brake firmly to reduce impact speed.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects your ability to stop. Slow down when roads are wet, icy, or in poor condition. Driving too fast on slippery roads makes it harder to stop and control your vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic light is ahead. Be ready to stop for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to turn left onto a highway or make a U-turn if allowed.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may move in the direction shown, if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must move in that direction, but only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must always stop completely before moving in that direction.
Drivers in that lane must move in that direction while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must move in that direction while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the pavement tells drivers in that lane they must move in the direction shown. Drivers must follow traffic signs and signals before proceeding in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal to the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes you on the left. Look for oncoming traffic and reduce your speed so the other vehicle can move back into the right lane easily.

questions.question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Go faster than traffic to get ahead.
Go slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.

questions.explanation: Highway entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. When merging, turn on your signal, look for an opening in traffic, speed up to match traffic, and merge into the opening.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive faster than the speed limit when passing another vehicle?
questions.explanation: You must never exceed the speed limit, even when passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. If you go too fast, your tires may lose grip entirely and slide on a film of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Each hard stop wastes fuel because you must accelerate again to reach traffic speed. Looking ahead and slowing down gradually, or changing lanes to avoid braking, saves fuel.

questions.question: When can drivers talk on cell phones while driving?
questions.explanation: You cannot hold a cell phone or handheld device while driving. You can talk on a cell phone only if you use a hands-free accessory. Text messaging while driving is never allowed.

questions.question: Your stopping distance increases when:

options.text: The road is wet or icy.
You are driving on paved highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is wet or icy.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances are longer on wet or icy roads. Stopping distances also increase on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow backgrounds and black letters. They alert drivers to hazards ahead.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow instructions are called:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. If you don't follow them, you can be penalized.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the road surface up to the top. Heat makes this worse.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means you cannot do that action. U-turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to:
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs mean you should yield. You can go when it is safe and the road is clear.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left, let oncoming cars and pedestrians go first. They have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What helps drivers avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to their vehicles to improve traction.
Get off the highways as quickly as possible.
Engage the four-wheel drive on their vehicles.
Reduce their speed and increase their following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed and increase their following distance.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow and ice. Keep more distance between your car and the car ahead. This is the best way to avoid crashes.

questions.question: Pennant-shaped signs indicate:
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mean you cannot pass other vehicles. The sign will say "No Passing Zone."

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before you turn or change lanes. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to get back on the road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.explanation: Let the bus merge back onto the road. Slow down, change lanes, or stop if needed to let it in safely.

questions.question: What colors are signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?
questions.explanation: Exit signs and direction signs are green with white letters or symbols.
